question: Why did the p95 latency go up on 16 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: The deployment of catalog v3.20 caused the increase in latency and request volume.
why_chain: The deployment of catalog v3.20 introduced changes that affected the system's performance.
The increase in request volume and error rate coincided with the deployment, indicating a possible correlation.
The autoscaler scaling out 4 new instances after the deployment suggests a system response to the increased load.

contributing_factors.description: The error rate increase could be due to the deployment's impact on system stability.
why_chain: The error rate increased after the deployment, suggesting a potential issue with the new version.
The deployment could have introduced bugs or changes that affected system stability.
The autoscaler scaling out new instances indicates the system was under stress.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in latency and request volume were due to a configuration change.
ruled_out.reason: No evidence supports a configuration change as the cause. The deployment of a new version is the most supported cause.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in latency and request volume were due to a data issue.
ruled_out.reason: No evidence supports a data issue. The increase in request volume and error rate are more aligned with system load and deployment impacts.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in latency and request volume were due to a dependency issue with an external service.
ruled_out.reason: No evidence supports a dependency issue. The deployment and increased load are more likely causes.

evidence.summary: P95 latency for region us-east rose from 137 ms to 270 ms (+97%), with a change point at 2026-03-16T04:40:00Z.
The change is concentrated in region us-east: 4 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.02).
At the same time, request volume for region us-east rose (2707 per 5 min before, 10491 per 5 min after, +288%).
At the same time, error rate for region us-east rose (0.40% before, 0.78% after, +97%).
Request volume 3x normal in us-east (us-east; 12 min after the change; record R009)
Deployed catalog v3.20 to us-east (routine release) (catalog, us-east; 126 min before the change; record R008)
autoscaler: scaling out, 4 new instances requested (us-east; 20 min after the change; record R010)

reasons: ✗ The closest change event is 126 min before the change, too far to be convincing.
✓ 2 log/alert record(s) after the change agree with the numbers.
✗ Request volume also rose, so a traffic explanation is still open.
✓ No competing change event fits as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.
missing_data: Change records from the hour before the change

actions.action: Roll back the catalog v3.20 deployment to revert the changes and observe the system's behavior.
Implement a load balancer to distribute the increased request volume more evenly across servers.
Monitor the system closely for any further issues and adjust the autoscaler as needed.
